raw_response:
Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-rays demonstrate marked tracheobronchomegaly (dilated trachea and main bronchi) and multiple large intrapulmonary cavities/cystic changes, which are hallmark radiographic features of Mounier-Kuhn syndrome. The progression to larger and more numerous cavities indicates disease advancement, necessitating management focused on airway clearance (physiotherapy) and treating superimposed infections with antibiotics.
